description: COREtec Plus Premium, with a 20 mil wear layer and cork back, is the best luxury vinyl plank for most homes. Seven brands compared by room and core.
dek: COREtec Plus Premium, with a 20 mil wear layer and cork back, is the best luxury vinyl plank for most homes.
intro: The best luxury vinyl plank flooring for most homes is COREtec Plus Premium, which pairs a 20 mil wear layer with an attached cork back for a floor that is tough, quiet and comfortable underfoot. For most rooms, the sweet spot is any rigid-core plank with a 12 to 20 mil wear layer and an attached pad.

The room changes the details. Kitchens, entries and homes with large dogs call for a 20 mil wear layer on a dense SPC core, bedrooms do fine with 12 mil, and basements depend on a moisture test and a vapor barrier. Below are seven lines ranked by the job they suit, then the questions buyers ask about wear layers, SPC vs WPC, waterproofing, installation and cost.
quickAnswer: COREtec Plus Premium is the best vinyl plank for comfort in main living areas. For heavy traffic choose Shaw Floorté Pro, for whole-house installs with kids and pets Mohawk SolidTech Plus, and on a budget a mid-tier Lifeproof or NuCore collection. Whatever the brand, buy a 12 to 20 mil wear layer and lay it over a flat subfloor.

blocks.p: Which brand of luxury vinyl planking is best depends on whether you value comfort, toughness, looks or cost. COREtec leads on comfort, Shaw and Mohawk on durability, Karndean on realism, and Lifeproof and NuCore on value.
Most of these names are families of collections, not single products. Always check the wear layer and warranty on the exact collection before you order.

sections.h: The 7 Best Luxury Vinyl Plank Flooring Brands in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: The ranking weighs published wear-layer thickness, core construction, attached underlayment, residential and commercial warranty terms, availability and recurring owner feedback about denting, gapping and locking joints. Specs come from manufacturer data sheets and retailer listings, not installs.

COREtec more or less created the rigid-core category, and Plus Premium is its comfort-first flagship. A thick WPC core is bonded to an attached cork underlayment, so the floor feels softer and sounds less hollow than most stone-core planks, a difference owners tend to notice once they live on it.

Per COREtec's specs, the 20 mil wear layer is suited to kitchens, family rooms and homes with pets. The planks come long and wide in a big color range, which keeps a room calm and leaves fewer seams to stagger. The thick core bridges small subfloor flaws better than thin planks, though the manufacturer's flatness tolerance still applies. The downsides are cost, near the top of the residential vinyl market, and a foamed core that can dent under narrow furniture feet and appliances unless you use wide coasters. If you want waterproof vinyl without the hard, clicky feel, start here.
**Pros:** 20 mil wear layer; attached cork back is quiet and warm; long, wide planks; thick core tolerates minor subfloor flaws; wide dealer network.
**Cons:** Priced at the top of the residential range; foamed core can dent under narrow heavy loads.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=COREtec+Plus+Premium+vinyl+plank&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Heavy Traffic: Shaw Floorté Pro

blocks.p: Floorté Pro is a family of Shaw rigid-core collections, and according to Shaw's published specs the better lines pair a dense SPC core with a 20 mil wear layer and light commercial warranty coverage. That combination makes it a strong choice for kitchens, mudrooms, home offices with rolling chairs and houses with big dogs, where dents and scuffs are the main threats.

SPC also moves less with temperature than a foamed core, which helps in sunrooms and on long open runs. The trade-off is feel: it is firmer than cork-backed WPC and can sound clicky over concrete, so check whether your collection has an attached pad. Because Floorté Pro spans many collections and price points, confirm the wear layer and warranty for the exact line. Shaw's wide distribution makes extra cartons easy to find later.
**Pros:** Dense stone core resists dents; 20 mil wear layer on many collections; light commercial warranties; stable in temperature swings.
**Cons:** Firm and can sound hard without a pad; specs vary by collection.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Shaw+Floort%C3%A9+Pro+vinyl+plank&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Most Durable All-Rounder: Mohawk SolidTech Plus

blocks.p: SolidTech Plus is Mohawk's tougher rigid-core line, with a thick top layer, attached underlayment and embossed wood visuals that hold up in daylight. It is built for whole-house installs, where one floor runs through the kitchen, hallway and living room without upgrading some rooms and not others.

Mohawk leans on pet-friendly performance, and owners commonly report it stands up well to claws and toys when furniture sits on felt pads. The attached pad cuts hollow sound and removes the need for separate underlayment over wood subfloors. Cartons weigh more than budget lines, a sign of a denser core and something to plan for if the flooring goes upstairs. Pricing sits in the middle to upper part of the market, and Mohawk sells several tiers under the SolidTech name, so check the wear layer and warranty for the collection you choose.
**Pros:** Thick top layer on many collections; attached pad; convincing embossed visuals; pet-focused warranties; widely sold.
**Cons:** Mid-to-upper pricing; heavier cartons.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Mohawk+SolidTech+Plus+vinyl+plank&tag=sktiger-20)

Karndean made its name with high-end glue-down vinyl, and Korlok Select brings that look to a click-lock rigid core. The visuals are the draw: varied grain, long boards and painted bevels that separate each plank the way real wood boards do, so the floor reads less like a repeating print.

Karndean lists a 20 mil wear layer for Korlok Select, which suits kitchens and living rooms, and the rigid core keeps floating installs straightforward for DIYers and pros. It costs more than most vinyl, often approaching engineered wood, and it is sold mainly through specialty flooring dealers rather than big-box shelves. For a renovation where the floor is the centerpiece and you still want vinyl's water tolerance in a kitchen or basement, it is the premium vinyl plank to shortlist.
**Pros:** Some of the most convincing wood looks in vinyl; 20 mil wear layer per Karndean; painted bevels; strong dealer support.
**Cons:** Expensive for vinyl; mostly sold through specialty dealers.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Karndean+Korlok+Select&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Pets: Pergo Extreme Rigid Core

blocks.p: Pergo is better known for laminate, but Pergo Extreme is its rigid-core vinyl line, marketed around resistance to pet accidents, scratches and spills. Most collections carry an attached pad, and Pergo's click system is designed to forgive first-time installers; owners commonly report the rows lock together cleanly.

Lowe's and other retailers stock it widely, so matching boards later for repairs is easy. The range spans several tiers, so compare wear layer and thickness per collection: a thicker wear layer for kitchens and dog households, a basic tier for bedrooms. As with all vinyl, the plank is waterproof but the installed floor is not a sealed pan, so clean up pet accidents promptly and seal the perimeter in wet rooms.
**Pros:** Pet and stain resistance is a design focus; attached pad on most collections; easy click joint; widely available.
**Cons:** Collections vary in wear layer and thickness; mid-range cost, not a budget line.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Pergo+Extreme+rigid+core+vinyl+plank&tag=sktiger-20)

Lifeproof is Home Depot's house brand of rigid-core vinyl, and availability is its biggest strength: you can see planks in person, take them home the same day and come back for more cartons from the same shelf. Most collections include an attached pad, so a wood subfloor needs no separate underlayment, though concrete still needs a vapor barrier.

The catch is that Lifeproof is an umbrella brand, with wear layers ranging from thin builder grades to thicker lines. Entry lines suit a bedroom or rental. For a kitchen or a dog-heavy living room, choose a collection with a 12 to 20 mil wear layer and pay the small difference. Owners commonly report an easy install and a few cracked tongues where joints were forced, so tap gently.
**Pros:** Low cost per square foot; attached pad; stocked in many colors; easy to buy extra cartons; simple click joint.
**Cons:** Wear layer varies widely by collection; thinner lines show subfloor flaws.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Lifeproof+rigid+core+vinyl+plank+flooring&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Budget Rigid Core: NuCore Performance

blocks.p: NuCore is Floor and Decor's in-house rigid-core brand, and its appeal is a cork back and SPC core at a cost well below national brands. The cork makes a stone core feel and sound noticeably softer, which answers the main complaint about SPC.

NuCore Performance spans many collections with different specs, so for main living areas pick a line with a 12 to 20 mil wear layer rather than the cheapest one. It is a sensible fit for basements, rental units and whole-floor projects where cost per square foot decides things. Owners commonly report an easy install and good looks for the money, while a few note the thinnest lines scuff in busy entries. Because only Floor and Decor sells it, buy enough for the job plus a spare carton, since dye lots and stock rotate.
**Pros:** Attached cork pad at a budget cost; SPC core for dent resistance; many collections in stock; good for basements and rentals.
**Cons:** Sold only through Floor and Decor; cheapest lines have thin wear layers.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=NuCore+Performance+vinyl+plank&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.h: What Wear Layer Thickness Do You Need?

blocks.p: Choose 12 mil for most living spaces and 20 mil for kitchens, entries, homes with large dogs and light commercial rooms. 6 to 8 mil is enough only for a guest room or closet, and anything above 20 mil is aimed at retail and office floors.

blocks.h3: Why total thickness is a poor guide

blocks.p: Cartons advertise total thickness in millimeters, and that number is mostly marketing. A 7 mm plank and a 5 mm plank with the same top layer wear at the same rate. What predicts scratch life is the wear layer, measured in mils (thousandths of an inch): the clear skin over the printed image. Once traffic grinds through it, the print wears and only a new plank fixes it.

Read the core separately. An 8 mm plank with a 1.5 mm attached pad is really a 6.5 mm board. A thicker rigid core bridges small dips more easily, but it is no excuse for a subfloor that is out of flat.
An attached cork or IXPE foam pad adds comfort and sound control and generally means no separate pad. A slab still needs the vapor barrier the maker specifies.

A lifetime residential warranty often excludes scratches, dents, fading and water from below. A 10- or 15-year light commercial rating says more about the surface than a lifetime residential headline.

sections.h: Is SPC or WPC Vinyl Plank Better?

blocks.p: SPC is better where dents are the threat; WPC is better where comfort and quiet matter more.

Powdered limestone blended with PVC and pressed into a dense board. It is heavy, hard and very stable, so it resists rolling chairs and furniture legs and barely moves with temperature. It feels firm and can sound clicky without a good pad. SPC dominates the budget and mid-range market and is the default for kitchens, basements and rentals. If you are asking what company makes the best SPC vinyl flooring, Shaw Floorté Pro is the strongest SPC line here, with NuCore and Lifeproof as value options.

WPC once meant wood plastic composite; today it describes a foamed PVC core that is thicker and lighter than SPC. It walks softer, warmer and quieter, which is why premium lines like COREtec use it. The foamed core dents more easily under concentrated weight, so use wide furniture cups and felt pads.

At 2 to 3 mm thick, glue-down plank needs a near-perfect substrate but handles commercial traffic, stairs and temperature swings, and planks can be replaced individually. Most DIY installers do better with click-lock rigid core.

Mineral and magnesium cores get fresh marketing names, but the same questions decide performance: dent resistance under load, wear layer thickness and how the locking joint survives years of movement.

sections.h: Which Vinyl Plank Is Best for Each Room?

blocks.p: SPC with a 20 mil wear layer in kitchens, 12 mil in bedrooms and living rooms, and a moisture test plus vapor barrier in the basement.

Pick an SPC core with at least a 20 mil wear layer and a tight angle-angle lock. Where allowed, run the floor into the dishwasher opening before the appliance goes in, and keep the specified gap at cabinets. Never fasten cabinets down through a floating floor.

Vinyl plank copes with a slightly damp slab if you lay the required vapor barrier. Test first: tape down an 18-inch square of plastic for 24 to 48 hours; condensation underneath means a moisture problem to fix. A [basement dehumidifier](/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) that holds humidity below about 55 percent protects the floor. If the walls weep, deal with them first; our [basement wall sealer guide](/best-basement-wall-sealer/) covers the options.
The planks will not swell, so vinyl suits bathrooms. Seal the perimeter at the tub and toilet with flexible silicone, and cut cleanly around the toilet flange rather than bolting through the plank.

Save money here. A 12 mil wear layer is plenty, and WPC or cork-backed SPC is quieter and warmer. In sunrooms, check the data sheet for a maximum temperature, since some cores expand enough in strong sun to peak at the joints.
Over radiant heat, confirm approval and keep the surface below the maker's limit, often around 85 degrees Fahrenheit. Three-season rooms need a product rated for unconditioned spaces.

sections.h: How Do You Install Click-Lock Vinyl Plank?

blocks.p: Get the subfloor flat, plan the layout, keep a quarter-inch gap at every edge, take the first two rows slowly and never force a joint.

Manufacturers typically call for flatness within 3/16 inch over 10 feet or 1/8 inch over 6 feet. Most failed vinyl floors fail at the joints, and most joint failures trace back to an uneven subfloor. Check with a long straightedge, fill dips with patch or self-leveler, and grind or sand high spots. Never float over carpet or cushioned vinyl.

You can usually float over firmly bonded, flat sheet vinyl or tile, but many floors laid before 1980 and their adhesives contain asbestos, so do not sand or scrape them until a sample is checked. Let cartons sit flat in the room for 24 to 48 hours at normal living temperature.

You need a utility knife, speed square, tapping block, pull bar, spacers, rubber mallet and jamb saw. Rigid cores score and snap. Plan so the last row is not a sliver, stagger end joints by 6 to 8 inches, and draw from three or four cartons at a time.
Leave about a quarter inch at walls, jambs, pipes and cabinets. Large open plans often need a transition at doorways or every 40 to 50 feet; check your product's maximum run.

Angle the long side in, drop the short end and tap lightly. Excess force cracks rigid-core tongues. If a joint will not close, unclick it and look for debris. Put felt pads under furniture before it returns.

sections.h: Is Vinyl Plank Flooring Really Waterproof?

blocks.p: The plank is waterproof; the installed floor is not. Waterproof on a carton means the plank will not swell or delaminate when water sits on it.

Water that runs into the perimeter gap or seeps between joints reaches the subfloor and stays there, trapped under a floor that will not let it dry. On plywood that means swelling, odor and mold long before the planks look damaged.

Many cover topical spills only. Flooding, hydrostatic pressure and water rising from below are usually excluded. Wipe spills promptly, and in bathrooms and laundry rooms run 100 percent silicone at the tub, shower and toilet.

Floating vinyl has one real advantage: you can unclick the planks, dry the subfloor with fans and a dehumidifier and often reinstall the same planks. A [shop vac](/best-shop-vac/) pulls standing water from the gap faster than towels. Keep a spare carton for that day.

Vinyl wins wherever water can sit or rise from a slab: basements, full baths, laundry rooms and mudrooms. Laminate's melamine top usually resists scratches better in dry rooms and feels closer to wood. Many homes use both, split by room. If your rooms are dry and pets are the main concern, compare our [laminate flooring picks](/best-laminate-flooring/) before ordering.

sections.h: How Much Does Luxury Vinyl Plank Cost, and How Long Does It Last?

blocks.p: Budget rigid-core lines cost the least, mid-range lines with a 12 to 20 mil wear layer and attached pad sit in the middle, and premium lines with thick wear layers, cork backs and long commercial warranties cost the most. Installation is a separate line item.

Installers commonly quote roughly $2 to $5 per square foot for click-lock vinyl, more when old flooring has to come out, the subfloor needs leveling or stairs are involved. Stairs are priced per step and take far longer. DIY saves the most in large, open rooms with simple layouts.

Order 7 to 10 percent extra for waste in simple rooms and 12 to 15 percent for rooms with many corners or a diagonal layout. Add transitions, quarter-round, a vapor barrier on concrete and floor patch, plus underlayment only if the plank has no pad.

Spend on wear layer and subfloor prep. Save on total thickness, bevel names and lifetime residential warranties that exclude almost everything. A 12 mil plank on a flat subfloor outlasts a 22 mil plank on a wavy one.

Over a flat, dry subfloor, a quality plank commonly lasts 15 to 25 years in a home, longer in quiet rooms. Thin wear layers in busy kitchens and entries can wear out in 5 to 10 years. Mats at every door, felt pads, a chair mat under rolling chairs and a damp mop with a vinyl cleaner extend its life. Avoid steam mops, oil soaps and rubber-backed rugs, which can yellow vinyl.

mistakes: Overall thickness says little about wear: a thick plank with a thin wear layer scuffs as fast as a thin one. Rank options by wear layer in mils, then core type, then thickness. In kitchens, entries and big-dog homes aim for 20 mil; the step up from 12 mil costs far less than a new floor.

A rigid core can hide a small bump but not a dip. When the subfloor is outside the maker's tolerance, the joints flex, the locks wear and gaps open within a year or two. Check with a long straightedge, fill low spots, grind high ones, and only then lay the first row.

Screwing kitchen islands, cabinets or heavy built-ins through a floating floor stops it from moving, and the stress shows up as peaked joints elsewhere. Install cabinets first and run the floor to them with a gap, or follow the maker's rules for heavy fixed loads.
Adding a second pad under attached underlayment

Planks with attached IXPE or cork are designed to sit directly on the subfloor or vapor barrier. A second foam layer makes the floor too soft, so the locking joints flex with every step until they break. On a slab, use only a thin poly vapor barrier unless the instructions say otherwise.
Trusting waterproof to protect the subfloor

Spills will not hurt the planks, but water that slips into the perimeter gap or a joint can soak the plywood below for weeks unseen. Caulk the edges of wet rooms with silicone, mop up spills quickly and repair leaks before they reach the subfloor.
bottomLine: COREtec Plus Premium is the best luxury vinyl plank flooring when you want a premium floor that is quiet and comfortable underfoot. Kitchens and pet households are best served by a 20 mil collection of Shaw Floorté Pro or Mohawk SolidTech Plus, Karndean Korlok Select earns its premium when realism matters most, and a mid-tier Lifeproof or NuCore line delivers most of the performance for far less. Whichever brand you choose, judge it by the wear layer, not the total thickness, and put your effort into the subfloor: a flat, dry base and an honest expansion gap add more years to the floor than any upgrade in the catalog.

faqs.q: What is the best luxury vinyl plank flooring?
faqs.a: COREtec Plus Premium is the best luxury vinyl plank for most main living areas, with a 20 mil wear layer and an attached cork back that makes it quiet and comfortable. Shaw Floorté Pro and Mohawk SolidTech Plus are tougher mid-range picks for kitchens and pets, and Lifeproof or NuCore mid-tier collections are the value choices.

faqs.q: Which brand of luxury vinyl plank is the highest rated?
faqs.a: COREtec, Shaw, Mohawk and Karndean are the most consistently well-regarded vinyl plank brands among owners and installers. COREtec leads on comfort, Shaw Floorté Pro and Mohawk SolidTech Plus on durability, and Karndean Korlok Select on realism. Ratings vary by collection, so check the wear layer of the exact line you buy.

faqs.q: What company makes the best SPC vinyl flooring?
faqs.a: Among these picks, Shaw Floorté Pro is the strongest SPC line, with a dense stone core, 20 mil wear layer on many collections and light commercial warranties. NuCore Performance adds a cork back to SPC at a budget cost, and Lifeproof offers SPC with an attached pad. Compare collections, since specs vary.

faqs.q: Is SPC or WPC vinyl plank better?
faqs.a: SPC is better for kitchens, basements, rentals and rooms with heavy furniture or rolling chairs, because its dense stone core resists dents and stays stable through temperature swings. WPC is better for bedrooms and family rooms where comfort and quiet matter, since its foamed core is softer and warmer underfoot.

faqs.q: How thick should the wear layer be on vinyl plank?
faqs.a: Choose 12 mil for most bedrooms and living spaces and 20 mil for kitchens, entries, hallways and homes with large dogs. 6 to 8 mil is enough only for closets and guest rooms. Surface life follows the wear layer, not the overall plank thickness printed on the carton.

faqs.q: Can you install vinyl plank flooring on a concrete slab?
faqs.a: Yes. Vinyl plank is one of the most forgiving floors for slabs, including basements. Test for moisture first, fill dips and grind high spots to meet the flatness tolerance, then lay the vapor barrier the manufacturer specifies, usually 6 mil poly with taped seams. Fix any active water problem before installing.

faqs.q: How long does luxury vinyl plank flooring last?
faqs.a: A quality vinyl plank laid over a flat, dry subfloor commonly lasts 15 to 25 years in a home, and longer in low-traffic rooms. Thin wear layers in busy kitchens and entries can wear through in 5 to 10 years. Door mats, felt pads and gentle cleaning add years to any vinyl floor.
